title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Jamf
providers.scope_notes: Covers Jamf (Jamf Pro, Jamf Platform API Gateway, Jamf Protect, Jamf School). Jamf Pro cloud (11.x) is the main focus; Jamf Log Stream export needs Jamf Cloud Premium; Protect and School covered from public docs only.

controls.name: Disable API Client
controls.what: Stops the client from issuing new access tokens; existing tokens stay valid until expiry.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > client > Disable API Client; or PUT /v1/api-integrations/{id} enabled=false

controls.name: Remove specified API integration
controls.what: Deletes the API client; already-issued tokens remain valid until expiry.

controls.name: Rotate Client Secret
controls.what: Invalidates the old secret so it can no longer mint tokens.
controls.setting: API client > Rotate Client Secret; POST /v1/api-integrations/{id}/client-credentials

controls.name: API Roles
controls.what: Client privileges are the union of assigned API roles; editing a role's privileges applies to live tokens immediately.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > API Roles; /v1/api-roles

controls.name: Access Token Lifetime
controls.what: Sets token lifetime in seconds per client; changes do not affect tokens already issued.

controls.name: Token scope parameter
controls.what: Caller may request a token limited to a subset of the client's roles.

no_control.what: Disabling or deleting an API client does not end access for tokens already issued; there is no documented per-client token revocation.

controls_unknown: IP allowlisting for Jamf Pro API clients or user API access (none found in public docs).

auth_paths.name: Jamf Pro API client (API Roles and Clients, client credentials)

authentication.summary: An admin creates an API client with one or more API roles and generates a client secret. The client ID and secret are exchanged at POST /api/v1/oauth/token (grant_type=client_credentials) for a short-lived bearer token. Works for both the Jamf Pro API and the Classic API.

federation.details: Static client secret; no workload identity federation documented. Jamf states API authentication does not support SSO.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for API clients found in public Jamf Pro docs.

lifetime.summary: Access token lifetime set per client (Access Token Lifetime, seconds); client secret has no documented expiry

renewal.summary: Request a new token with the same client ID and secret; secret is rotated manually.

administration.summary: Settings > System > API roles and clients. Admins can disable, delete, or rotate the secret of a client and edit its roles. Managed by API at /v1/api-integrations and /v1/api-roles.

sso.details: Jamf says API authentication does not support SSO; client credentials are exchanged directly for tokens.

offboard.details: API clients are standalone service credentials, not tied to a Jamf Pro user account.

inventory.details: Settings > API Roles and Clients lists clients; GET /v1/api-integrations returns them via API.

reads.ui: Jamf Pro > Settings > System > Change management (Read operations); Jamf Cloud Premium: stream JAMFChangeManagement via Jamf Log Stream

token_format.notes: Client ID is a UUID; access token is a JWT (sample token in docs is a three-part eyJ... JWT with scope api-role:N).

log_sources.name: Change Management log
log_sources.notes: Settings > Change Management; Jamf Cloud: view in UI only, not exportable except via Jamf Log Stream (Jamf Cloud Premium). Retention set by log flushing.

log_sources.name: Access Log
log_sources.notes: Login and token requests with username, IP, entryPoint. Export via Log Stream (Premium). Flushable.

log_sources.name: RestAPIOperation webhook
log_sources.notes: Fires on authorized Classic API requests; includes authorizedUsername, objectTypeName, restAPIOperationType.

credential_id_fields.notes: Client ID of the API client.
What value appears for an API client is not documented.

anomaly_cues: New API client or newly rotated secret
Role with broad privileges added to a client
Classic API reads from unexpected sources via RestAPIOperation webhook

containment.steps: Disable or delete the client and rotate its secret; to cut live tokens immediately, remove privileges from the client's API roles (role changes apply to live tokens).
containment.notes: Disable/delete leaves valid tokens working until expiry; role edits apply immediately.

unknown: Exact Change Management event names for API client actions
Whether client-credential token requests are recorded in the Access Log

calls.log_notes: Change Management records READ operations for some objects; not confirmed for API reads.

calls.reveals: FileVault recovery data for all computers

calls.log_notes: Change Management log records Read operations (shown as [READ] entries with username). In Jamf Cloud it is viewable in the UI only; export via Log Stream needs Jamf Cloud Premium.

unknown: GET /v1/auth behavior for client-credential tokens (documented for user tokens)
